subject: Intermittent latency spike impacting checkout - request for SLA remedy
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@klyro.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: support@klyro.com
Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency spike impacting checkout - request for SLA remedy

Hi Camila,

We saw a significant latency spike affecting our checkout flow this morning between 02:41:00 and 02:55:30 UTC (US-WEST-2 region). During that window our p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s and our p99 regularly breached 5s; a handful of requests returned 503. This increased cart abandonment by approximately 3.7% on our side (we can share platform metrics if helpful).

Can you confirm whether that window is eligible for an SLA credit? We need: a) confirmation of the affected availability window from Redwood's telemetry, b) a copy of any initial telemetry/trace bundle you have, and c) an ETA for a postmortem.

I've attached a ZIP with screenshots and our request IDs (klyro-req-5567, klyro-req-5568). We are in the middle of a big sale and this is material for our Q3 numbers, so a timely response would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Director of Engineering, Klyro
maya.patel@klyro.com

Attachments: klyro_checkout_screenshots.zip

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com

Hi Maya — thanks for the details and the screenshots. I'm looping in Diego (SRE) and Laura (AM) to help validate telemetry and start the incident workflow.

Quick ask from our side to speed validation: can you paste a sample request ID and approximate client timestamp in UTC for one or two failed requests (you listed two IDs; if you can include an exact timestamp for klyro-req-5567 that will help correlate traces)? Also let us know whether the affected customers were routed to any custom model variants or private pools.

Next steps from us: Diego will pull the runtime traces and an initial timeline, we'll confirm the exact impact window, and we'll propose a provisional credit calculation within 24 hours. We'll also open a formal incident ticket and schedule a postmortem; Laura will coordinate the meeting.

—Camila

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2029 14:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike impacting checkout - request for SLA remedy

Hi team — I pulled the initial traces for US-WEST-2 and correlated host telemetry. Preliminary findings:

- Impact window: 2029-06-07T02:40:52Z -> 2029-06-07T02:55:28Z (matches Klyro timestamps).
- Symptom: sudden p99 latency increase with a subset of requests returning 503s.
- Root cause (initial): a burst of preemptions on several autoscaled GPU pods triggered a short period of queueing while warmup completed; persistent KV-cache misses increased per-token work.

I attached a compressed trace bundle (trace_bundle_usw2_20290607.tar.gz) and a short log extract (first/last 500 lines per host). The traces include per-request routing decisions and kernel selection logs — there are clear handoffs where requests were retried to fallback variants during the window.

Recommendation:
- Open standard incident postmortem (I will own the RCA writeup).
- Confirm SLA eligibility subject to contract terms: this looks like a service availability/latency breach caused by infrastructure preemption. I believe Klyro is eligible for proportional credit; I'll calculate the prorated amount after full trace reconciliation.

I'll continue digging into autoscaler events and warmup timing. If legal/accounting needs a provisional number sooner, I can produce a rough calc by end of day.

—Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Attachments: trace_bundle_usw2_20290607.tar.gz

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@klyro.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 8 Jun 2029 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike impacting checkout - request for SLA remedy

Hi Maya — thanks for your patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

1) Impact window confirmed: 2029-06-07T02:40:52Z through 2029-06-07T02:55:28Z (Redwood telemetry correlated with Klyro request IDs).
2) Ticket opened: REDWOODINC-21873 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/REDWOODINC-21873).
3) Cause (preliminary): autoscaler preemption + KV-cache warmup leading to transient queueing and higher p99. Diego is preparing the RCA and full trace reconciliation.
4) Provisional remedy: we put together a provisional credit calc (attached provisional_credit_calc.xlsx) based on the measured availability delta and your committed service tier. Final credit will be confirmed after we complete the postmortem and reconcile traces.

We'd like to schedule a 45-minute postmortem review next week (options: Tue 2029-06-11 14:00 UTC or Wed 2029-06-12 09:00 UTC). Please let us know which works for your team and whether you'd like a deeper dive into kernel selection and cache-warmup behavior.

Again — apologies for the disruption during your sale event. We're treating this as high priority and will share the RCA and raw logs via the linked Drive folder as soon as Diego completes the extraction.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: provisional_credit_calc.xlsx
